title: Generic constancy of geometric reducedness on an irreducible base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. For $y\in Y$ regard the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] as a scheme over its residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. There exists a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in V$, $X_y$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$ if and only if $X_\eta$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. In particular both alternatives, geometrically reduced and not geometrically reduced generic fibre, are included. No flatness, reducedness of $Y$, Noetherianity or nonemptiness of the fibres is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0578 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-generic-fibre) and 0577 (lemma-not-geometrically-reduced-in-neighbourhood): apply 0578 when the generic fibre is geometrically reduced, and 0577 otherwise. Both source lemmas assume only finite type; the quasi-compact locally finitely presented case here is a specialization.

proof.text: Because $f$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], it is locally of finite type: a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated, and the condition passes to every affine open of $Y$ by restricting to principal opens common to two affine opens. Since $f$ is moreover quasi-compact, it is of finite type by the definition of finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This verifies the finiteness hypothesis of Tags 0577 and 0578 without adding flatness, reducedness, Noetherianity, or a nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Tags 0577 and 0578 hypotheses; finite type definition as quasi-compact and locally of finite type

proof.text: Use excluded middle on the proposition that the generic fibre $X_\eta$ is geometrically reduced. If it is geometrically reduced, apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-geometrically-reduced-open] to obtain a nonempty open $V$ on which every fibre is geometrically reduced, hence each fibre has the same truth value as the generic fibre. If it is not geometrically reduced, apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-not-geometrically-reduced-open] to obtain a nonempty open $V$ on which every fibre is not geometrically reduced, again giving the stated equivalence. The fibre notation and the geometric-reducedness predicates are exactly those in the item, so the argument also covers empty fibres.
